descriptionPlain:
Waabi, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we're unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that's powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech.
With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai


As a Electrical Engineer, you will be responsible for turning our custom electronics from a design file into road-ready hardware. You'll partner with our contract manufacturers to get boards built and then work with technicians to validate, program and assemble them, ready to be installed on our autonomous vehicles. You will also be responsible for ensuring the quality of our designs by designing test fixtures and working on Verification and Validation efforts.  On top of all that, when something doesn't behave the way the schematic says it should, you'll be getting your hands dirty as the one with the soldering iron, the scope, and the terminal open.
This is an onsite position to be based in Pittsburgh with the expectations of 3-4 days onsite.
You Will…
CM Coordination: Work directly with our Contract Manufacturers (CMs) to get PCBs and assemblies manufactured. You'll shepherd builds through fabrication, follow up on schedules, and flag issues before they become bottlenecks.
Incoming Inspection & Assembly: Collaborate with our quality management team to develop controls and monitors of our embedded hardware products at various stages of manufacture. You’ll work with our technicians to inspect received boards for quality and workmanship issues, perform rework and hand-assembly as needed, test and validate boards and then integrate into their final enclosures. And of course, you’ll make sure we comply with our OEM partner and internal quality standards.
Inventory Management: Track components, boards, and assemblies so the team always knows what's on hand, what's in transit, and what needs reordering.
End-of-Line (EOL) Debug: Support vehicle end-of-line testing by helping diagnose and resolve board- and vehicle-level issues. 
Test Fixture Design & Module V&V: You’ll work with our design and V&V teams to develop module end-of-line test fixtures, which you’ll then use to evaluate our designs under nominal and stressful environmental and electrical conditions.
Qualifications:
The Credentials: BS/MS in Electrical Engineering or a related field. You’ve likely spent 10+ years in hardware development and/or test engineering, with at least 2-3 years in a formal leadership role.
CMFluency: You speak the language of CMs. You understand how to partner with them to deliver a high quality product.
The "Maker" Mindset: You aren't afraid to get your hands dirty in the lab, but you have the strategic vision to step back and manage the high-level roadmap.
Process Improver: You are always looking for ways to improve our designs, our processes, and the ways we work.
